subject.title: feat: replace legacy exec approvals with V2

question: Should this release intentionally invalidate existing Windows V1 command-text allow and deny policy state, and remove string-form raw `system.run` compatibility, or should it ship a constrained compatibility and migration path?
rationale: Both behaviors can be implemented safely, but deciding whether existing authorization state and public caller contracts may break is a security and release-policy choice that source inspection cannot resolve.

options.title: Add constrained compatibility
options.body: Translate established string-form callers at the node boundary and provide a reviewed migration or visible V2 reapproval path for V1 policy users.

options.title: Approve a breaking security cutover
options.body: Accept argv-only input and V1 policy retirement for this release with explicit upgrade notes and operator recovery guidance.

recommendation.title: Add constrained compatibility
recommendation.body: Translate established string-form callers at the node boundary and provide a reviewed migration or visible V2 reapproval path for V1 policy users.

likelyOwner.reason: The current implementation contributor documented and implemented the cutover behavior, making them the clearest routing point for the decision record.
